newsitem.title: USA: Ford to idle 4 car plants next week.
newsitem.headline: Ford to idle 4 car plants next week.

text.p: Slow car sales have prompted Ford Motor Co to idle four North American plants next week, the automaker said on Thursday.

Ford will idle its Cuautitlan, Mexico, and Kansas City Assembly plants that make the Contour and Mystique sedans, affecting a total of 3,100 workers. The plants normally produce about 4,500 of the cars a week.
Also idled will be Ford's Wayne, Mich., stamping and assembly plant that normally produces 5,900 Escort and Tracer small cars a week. About 3,200 workers will be affected.
The company's Lorain car assembly operation in Lorain, Ohio, will be down in a move that idles 1,800 workers. The plant typically makes 3,200 Thunderbird and Cougar coupes a week.
All of the car plants are scheduled to resume normal operations April 14.
The U.S. No. 2 automaker is running both daily and Saturday overtime at numerous U.S. and Canadian light truck plants.
General Motors Corp has scheduled overtime for several light truck plants for the week of April 7. The company said it had not scheduled any downtime.
Chrysler Corp said eight of its nine U.S. assembly plants and all three Canadian assembly plants will operate the week of April 7.
